top20.name: Nine Way 玖味 / Noodle Nine 玖面
Facing East Taiwanese 東來食府

prospects.name: Hui Lau Shan (Redmond)
prospects.personalization_hook: Reportedly the Hong Kong brand's first US outpost, and the entire menu is fruit-driven
prospects.scoring_note: Produce price and peak timing hit them harder than almost anyone on the Eastside — fruit IS their P&L. Runs its own location Instagram, so a local operator.

prospects.name: Tasty Szechuan 蜀府宴语
prospects.personalization_hook: Posts to Instagram as @tastyszechuan under the Chinese name 蜀府宴语 — a bilingual feed you can write captions straight into
prospects.scoring_note: Best overall fit found: produce-intensive, already runs weekday specials, own site AND own Instagram. Bilingual opener safe.

prospects.name: Nine Way 玖味 / Noodle Nine 玖面
prospects.personalization_hook: Runs two brands out of the identical suite at 14808 NE 24th St A, so menu decisions serve two storefronts at once
prospects.scoring_note: Multi-brand operator feels the pain twice. Chengdu-style Sichuan.

prospects.name: Dong Ting Chun
prospects.personalization_hook: The same group just opened Spring Bistro in Bothell as a next-generation concept — they are actively developing new menus right now
prospects.scoring_note: Hunan = chili and fresh-vegetable driven. Group in active menu-development mode.

prospects.name: Spring Bistro 晓春舍
prospects.personalization_hook: A brand-new tapas-format concept from the next generation of the Dong Ting Chun family group
prospects.scoring_note: Small-plates format is the easiest place to slot a rotating seasonal dish. Brand new = menu still being formed.

prospects.name: Chan's Place
prospects.personalization_hook: Their own site has promised 'fresh local produce' since 1980 — and there is nothing seasonal on the menu to back it up
prospects.scoring_note: The gap between the claim and the menu IS the pitch, in one sentence. Family-owned since Aug 1980.

prospects.name: Made In Taiwan (food trailer)
prospects.personalization_hook: As a trailer they re-announce where they are every week — already posting schedule-plus-menu content constantly
prospects.scoring_note: Highest content cadence need in the set. Sells a Taiwanese train bento; has vegan/vegetarian options.

prospects.name: 151 Days
prospects.personalization_hook: Already runs a seasonal special menu, built by a chef who came from hotel kitchens in Taiwan
prospects.scoring_note: THE strongest lead in the territory: the only business that has already committed to seasonality. Do not sell the concept — sell the sourcing work behind it.

prospects.name: Rice & Noodles Chinese Kitchen
prospects.personalization_hook: A food-court stall competing on portion size and value — cheaper seasonal produce goes straight to margin
prospects.scoring_note: Tofu substitution on most mains = produce-flexible. 30 reviews, micro-operation.

prospects.name: Sichuanese Cuisine
prospects.personalization_hook: Plates family-style for two or more and carries a real vegetarian sub-menu — unusual for a Sichuan house here
prospects.scoring_note: Vegetable-forward Sichuan: string beans, mapo, veggie subs. Own site. Strong fit.

prospects.name: Frying Fish
prospects.personalization_hook: Built a separate takeout-only domain, fryingfishtogo.com — takeout is where their menu decisions land
prospects.scoring_note: Chilies, pickled vegetables, aromatics. Owns own channel.

prospects.name: Dumpling The Noodle (Kirkland)
prospects.personalization_hook: About half their menu is vegan, and they take part in Seattle Restaurant Week
prospects.scoring_note: Half-vegan menu = heavy, rotating vegetable sourcing. Same brand as P1-13 (Seattle) — one owner, two locations, contact once.

prospects.name: Duyen Hai Market
prospects.personalization_hook: Sits in the same 164th St SW strip as Mount & Bao — a grocer and a Hunan kitchen sharing a parking lot
prospects.scoring_note: Only small independent grocer found in the whole Eastside territory. Produce is the core of the business.

prospects.name: Kiki Bakery & Cafe
prospects.personalization_hook: Bakes handmade Taiwanese breads daily and pours teas sourced from Taiwan
prospects.scoring_note: Fruit seasonality maps directly onto cake and drink specials. Daily bake = constant menu decisions.

prospects.name: Facing East Taiwanese 東來食府
prospects.personalization_hook: Sells Taiwanese bento boxes alongside the bao burgers
prospects.scoring_note: Bento format is the easiest place to slot a rotating seasonal side. Two locations, owner-run.

prospects.name: Early Bird Cafe
prospects.personalization_hook: Reported to be under new management with a refreshed menu
prospects.scoring_note: A transition moment — someone is actively rethinking the board right now. Best timing signal in the set.

prospects.name: August Moon Chinese Restaurant
prospects.personalization_hook: Their own copy frames the business around serving 'Issaquah and Sammamish neighbors' fresh food
prospects.scoring_note: Same claim-vs-static-menu gap as Chan's Place. Hyperlocal identity a local-produce sheet plugs into.

prospects.name: Dan Gui Sichuan Cuisine
prospects.personalization_hook: Signature is stir-fried pork with pepper — a dish whose character depends on which chilies are good that week
prospects.scoring_note: Pepper-and-vegetable led. On Chowbus rather than own domain.

prospects.name: Xiang House
prospects.personalization_hook: Hunan is still a thin category on the Eastside — leads on smoky wok aroma and signature rice noodles
prospects.scoring_note: Hunan = chili, garlic, fresh vegetable driven. Site says 'made fresh every day'. Own ordering domain.

prospects.name: Spicy Talk Bistro
prospects.personalization_hook: Hand-shaven noodles and scratch-made sauces; the original Redmond Way location closed while Kirkland carries on
prospects.scoring_note: Produce-intensive Sichuan, own site, owner-run schedule (closed Mondays).

prospects.name: Mount & Bao 潇湘阁
prospects.personalization_hook: They make dim sum by hand on top of a Hunan and Sichuan menu — two labour-heavy programmes in one strip-mall kitchen

prospects.name: Lulu Mart
prospects.personalization_hook: One of the newer Chinatown grocers, opening as Rising Produce and Vy's Produce closed off Jackson
prospects.scoring_note: Produce IS the perishable inventory. Highest waste-reduction fit. No contact surfaced.

prospects.name: Dong Hing Market
prospects.personalization_hook: Still open on Jackson after Rising Produce closed and Vy's was redeveloped — it absorbed that produce demand
prospects.scoring_note: Fresh produce and meat. Independent corner grocer, 29 reviews.

prospects.name: Supreme Dumplings
prospects.personalization_hook: Their menu already carries a 'Stir Fried Seasonal Greens with Garlic' line item
prospects.scoring_note: An existing seasonal slot a 节气 sheet can fill with no menu redesign. But ~1,979 reviews and an 877 call-centre number — busy, harder to reach a decision-maker.

prospects.name: Miah's Kitchen
prospects.personalization_hook: Runs a Chinese breakfast service — youtiao and soy milk — on top of the Xi'an hand-pulled noodle menu
prospects.scoring_note: Two dayparts to fill. No own website.

prospects.name: Seattle Dumpling
prospects.personalization_hook: Operates out of stall 14 at Pike Place, steps from the market's own produce vendors
prospects.scoring_note: The most literal 'what is peaking locally' pitch in the whole list. Micro-operation.

prospects.name: Little Ting's Dumplings
prospects.personalization_hook: Pork & chive is the signature and they carry vegan dumplings too
prospects.scoring_note: Filling vegetables are a real weekly variable input. Own branded ordering site.

prospects.name: Sweet Dream Bakes
prospects.personalization_hook: Her profile frames the desserts around culture, memory and belonging
prospects.scoring_note: Solo operator, Instagram IS the menu — needs postable seasonal content constantly. Only verifiable Instagram-native operator found.

prospects.name: Cafe Aloe
prospects.personalization_hook: Their piggy buns are the item people photograph
prospects.scoring_note: Already leans on visual postable items. Specialty-drink program is the natural seasonal slot.

prospects.name: Origin Bakery
prospects.personalization_hook: Bakes out of Eastside Commissary Kitchen in Redmond, sells via pickup drops announced on Instagram; signature is the 'Crochi' mochi croissant
prospects.scoring_note: Two named founders, commissary model, Instagram-announced drops. Constant need for postable content.

prospects.name: Chuan House
prospects.personalization_hook: Named their domain after the UW campus — the business runs on the student calendar
prospects.scoring_note: Sichuan = produce-intensive. Student calendar means demand swings, so over-buying is a live problem.

prospects.name: S-Mart Asian Supermarket
prospects.personalization_hook: Positions on a selection of organic and natural foods, unusual for a small Asian grocer here
prospects.scoring_note: Produce is the perishable inventory driving waste and turnover.

prospects.name: Asian Kitchen 德记
prospects.personalization_hook: Keeps 德记 alongside the English name, closed Tuesdays — a one-kitchen operation
prospects.scoring_note: Own single-restaurant ordering domain. Bilingual framing safe. Broad small-plate menu.

prospects.name: Young's Restaurant
prospects.personalization_hook: Runs an American breakfast menu and a Chinese/Thai menu out of one kitchen
prospects.scoring_note: Cross-menu operation buys produce for both. Multi-gen Cantonese-American: use English.

prospects.name: Dumpling The Noodle
prospects.personalization_hook: Advertises both handmade Northern dumplings and hand-pulled lamen made in house
prospects.scoring_note: Two labour-heavy items in one small kitchen.

prospects.name: Fang's Noodle House 芳饺子馆
prospects.personalization_hook: Their only real publishing channel is an Instagram account, not a website
prospects.scoring_note: No website — the captions half of the pack is worth more to them than the menu half.

prospects.name: Tian Tian Noodles 天天面
prospects.personalization_hook: Noodles cut by hand in small batches; appears to have moved from NE 24th St to a downtown Redmond storefront
prospects.scoring_note: Own ordering site — does its own menu maintenance.

prospects.name: Hakka House 興客軒
prospects.personalization_hook: The owner closed the Bellevue location, moved to Hawaii, then came back to reopen in Redmond
prospects.scoring_note: Menu spans the Hakka diaspora — Cantonese dim sum plus Fujian and Taiwanese.

prospects.name: J & J Chinese Restaurant
prospects.personalization_hook: Their own site positions them as serving three cities at once from one small Gilman Blvd suite

prospects.name: Seattle Dumpling House
prospects.personalization_hook: Serves dumplings until 3:30am — The Infatuation titled its review '3am dumplings are within reach'
prospects.scoring_note: Great hook, no contact surfaced. High turnover.

prospects.name: Tai Tung Chinese Restaurant
prospects.personalization_hook: Bruce Lee's table is still there; his order, oyster sauce beef, is a house signature
prospects.scoring_note: Legacy 1935 restaurant, 3rd-gen family. Famous fixed menu = low menu-change appetite, but real produce cost. Strongest personalization hook in the set.

prospects.name: 100th Ave Cakes
prospects.personalization_hook: Runs the whole business off a Facebook page from a home kitchen — captions are literally their storefront
prospects.scoring_note: Closest thing found to a 私房 operator. Agent confidence 0.78.

prospects.name: Seattle Chinese Herb & Grocery
prospects.personalization_hook: An herb shop is the one retailer where 节气 framing is already native to how customers shop
prospects.scoring_note: Dried + fresh. The 节气 frame needs no explaining here.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Best Wok
prospects.personalization_hook: Third-generation chef-owner Dennis has been reworking the family recipes at a restaurant open since 1984
prospects.scoring_note: Documented, specific hook. No direct contact surfaced.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Biang Biang Noodles
prospects.personalization_hook: Moved into the space the well-known Taiwanese restaurant Facing East used to occupy on Redmond Way
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Imperial Wok
prospects.personalization_hook: Closes 2-4pm daily and is done by 8pm — a small family crew with no website
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Macky's Dim Sum
prospects.personalization_hook: After years in Gilman Village they moved into the old Cloud 9 Lounge space — a bar room, not a purpose-built dim sum room
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Asian Wok
prospects.personalization_hook: They maintain two nearly identical self-built ordering sites — someone in the business does their own web and menu work
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Yummy House Bakery
prospects.personalization_hook: Open since 1998 and positions on 'healthy' cakes and buns rather than the standard HK bakery pitch
prospects.scoring_note: Fruit-based, not vegetable. Own site.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: A Ma Chicken Rice
prospects.personalization_hook: The whole business is built around one dish, so sides and specials are where any variety has to come from
prospects.scoring_note: Single-dish focus limits produce upside.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Golden Daisy 永盛
prospects.business_type: Dim sum + Cantonese BBQ, takeout only
prospects.personalization_hook: Cash-only, to-go-only counter that still keeps 永盛 on its own self-built site
prospects.scoring_note: Protein-fixed. Self-built Weebly = owner controls own channel, a documented buying signal. Pitch turnover, not menu.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Sichuan Cuisine (Redmond)
prospects.scoring_note: Good category fit, nothing verified to personalize with.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Dong Sing Market
prospects.scoring_note: Tiny (12 reviews). Great category fit, nothing to personalize with yet.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Taste of Xian
prospects.personalization_hook: Makes real hand-pulled noodles in house and markets on Shaanxi regional cooking, not generic Chinese
prospects.scoring_note: Noodle-fixed with vegetable-heavy cold dishes. No contact surfaced.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Great China Restaurant
prospects.personalization_hook: Over 30 years in the same family, and no website of their own — only aggregator listings
prospects.scoring_note: Agent confidence 0.70. Listings disagree on whether it is Kirkland or Redmond Way. Verify before contacting.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: U Lin Asian Bistro
prospects.personalization_hook: Own site calls them a 'family operated neighborhood Chinese restaurant' doing dim sum next to General Tso's
prospects.scoring_note: Agent confidence 0.65 — shares an address with Mount & Bao; one may have replaced the other. Verify before contacting.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Jade Garden
prospects.personalization_hook: Named to The Infatuation's 2025 list of the 25 best restaurants in the CID
prospects.scoring_note: 1,971 reviews. Too busy to read cold mail.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Mike's Noodle House
prospects.personalization_hook: Congee with a Chinese donut is the ordering ritual locals push
prospects.scoring_note: 1,568 reviews — busy enough to ignore cold outreach. Fixed protein/noodle menu.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.name: Red Pepper
prospects.scoring_note: Good category fit, no contact, no hook. Needs enrichment before it is contactable.
prospects.why_not: low fit or nothing verified to personalize with

prospects.scoring_note: Nothing verified to personalize with.

prospects.name: Dim Sum King
prospects.personalization_hook: Opens 7am, closed Wednesdays — an early-morning dim sum counter, not cart service
prospects.scoring_note: Fixed dumpling lineup, low produce. High turnover. No public contact found.

prospects.name: Ton Kiang Barbeque Noodle House
prospects.personalization_hook: Closes at 6pm — roast duck and crispy pork sold by the pound during the day
prospects.scoring_note: Protein-fixed, owner couple. Pitch inventory turnover only.

prospects.personalization_hook: Also trades as King's Kitchen on aggregators — a small ID dim sum house, not a banquet hall
